Svāhā. Fifteenth: If there are good sons or good daughters who are able to recite this mantra, Amitābha Buddha will constantly abide upon their crowns, protecting them day and night so that no enemies may find an opportunity against them. In this present life they shall always attain peace and security, and at the time of death, they will be reborn spontaneously in the Pure Land.
*The Biography of the Inconceivable Supernatural Power of the Amitābha Sūtra*, appended to the Sui Records; the author is unknown.

Formerly, there were Dharma Master Sengrui of Chang’an, Hui-chong, Seng-xian, and Hui-tong; more recently, up to the time of the Later Zhou, there were Shi Chan-shi, Jing Chan-shi, Dharma Master Luan of Xihe, and several hundred others, all of whom were reborn in the Western Land.

Upon seeing that Dharma Master Luan had attained rebirth in the Pure Land, the Chan Master Chuo of the West River and others each led those with whom they shared a karmic affinity to single-mindedly cultivate the practices for the Pure Land;
furthermore, Master Chuo compiled a record of verified accounts of the Western Paradise, titled the *Anle ji* (Collection on Peaceful Bliss), which circulated widely.

Furthermore, during the Jin dynasty, Dharma Master Huiyuan entered Mount Lu and did not emerge for thirty years; he then summoned one hundred and twenty-three of his like-minded companions, both monastics and laypeople, to take an oath directed toward the Western Land, carving inscriptions into the mountain to manifest their vows.

During the Tianjia era of the Chen dynasty, Master Lu Shan-zhen saw several hundred people while sitting in meditation, all traveling together on a flower-boat made of the seven treasures toward the Western Quarter; Master Shan-zhen then requested to be allowed to board.

The people on the boat replied, "Although you, Dharma Master, have mastered the preaching of the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, this is nonetheless a most inconceivable matter; since you have not yet memorized the *Amitābha Sūtra* and its dhāraṇī, you may not go with us."

The Dharma Master consequently abandoned his lecture duties and devoted himself day and night exclusively to reciting the *Amitābha Sūtra* and dharanis, totaling approximately twenty thousand recitations.

Less than twenty-eight days before the end of his life, at the fourth watch of the night, a divine being arrived from the west, bringing a white silver platform that appeared in the air with a brilliance surpassing the sun. It announced:
"When the Dharma Master’s life ends, you shall ascend this platform and be reborn in the Land of Amitābha; I have come to show this to you so that you may know your rebirth is certain."
At the time of his passing, both monastics and laypeople heard the sound of music playing in the air and smelled an extraordinary fragrance that did not cease for several months.
That night, the monks at the summit temple all saw dozens of torches, as large as chariot wheels, within a valley.

Examining the past and present, one finds that those who have attained rebirth in the World of Peace and Bliss are not few; many have witnessed auspicious omens such as transformation Buddhas and their assemblies coming to welcome them, as recorded in various traditions like the *Guangming*, which cannot be cited here in exhaustive detail.

Because Chan Master Yinchen experienced a miraculous response regarding this sutra, I have briefly recorded this one passage to enlighten future generations and assist them in their aspiration for rebirth in the Pure Land.

As for the "Divine Mantra for Eradicating the Root of All Karmic Obstacles and Attaining Rebirth in the Pure Land," it was translated by Guṇabhadra under imperial decree during the final years of the Yuanjia era of the Song dynasty; it consists of fifty-nine characters in fifteen phrases.
The Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna vowed to be reborn in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (Sukhāvatī) and was moved by this dhāraṇī in a dream.

The Tripiṭaka Master Yaśas recited this dhāraṇī, and Dharma Master Xiù of Tiānpíng Monastery received it orally from the Tripiṭaka Master Yaśas. That person said: "The original sūtra has not come from foreign lands;

however, if you wish to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī method, you should chew willow twigs and wash with soap powder, rinse your mouth, and burn incense. Then, kneeling on your right knee before an image of the Buddha with palms joined, recite it twenty-one times during each of the six periods of the day and night. Thus, the offenses of the four grave pārājika transgressions, the five heinous crimes, the ten evil deeds, and the slander of the Vaipulya sūtras shall all be extinguished and completely eliminated."
Whatever one seeks in this present life shall be attained, and one will not be deluded or disturbed by evil spirits or ghosts.

If the count reaches two hundred thousand recitations, one will immediately experience the sprouting of the tooth of Bodhi; if it reaches three hundred thousand recitations, one will behold Amitābha Buddha face-to-face.
"Thus [he said]."
